jobs.title: Sales Operations & Strategy Manager - Emerging Midmarket
jobs.description:
Emerging Mid-Market is one of QuickBooks’ highest-leverage growth bets — a fast-growing, multi-channel motion spanning inbound and outbound, account-based hunting, upgrades and migrations, and the Advanced product line. The growth has outpaced the operating infrastructure built to manage it. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and operations: defining who we target, designing the plays that win them, tracking what those plays produce, and translating it all into a revenue view that leadership and Finance trust. It is equal parts strategist and operator — analytical enough to be trusted with the numbers, strategic enough to do something useful with them.

Responsibilities
Strategy & GTM
- Define and refine ICPs, customer segmentation, and market sizing to drive EMM targeting and coverage

- Design, launch, and measure Go-to-Market plays end to end — bringing a clear double-down / modify / cut recommendation

- Develop new initiative concepts grounded in propensity, conversion, capacity, and competitive signal

Performance Tracking & Sales Operations

- Build and maintain a Finance-reconciled units-to-revenue view, plus durable forecasting and capacity models

- Flag initiative risk early — with root cause and recommendation — before quarter end, not after

Cross-Functional & Executive

- Drive adoption of new tools, reports, and processes across the team

The strongest candidates bring the operating toolkit of a top-tier management consulting firm — and the judgment to apply it in-house, inside a fast-moving sales organization.

- Exceptional AI GTM fluency -- knows and have experience running agentic AI GTM stack using state of the art tools & framework beyond chat (e.g., Claude Code, Cowork, Codex, Antigravity)

jobs.description:

jobs.title: Staff Program Manager, Organizational Change Management
jobs.description:
Intuit's CTREC organization (Cybersecurity, Trust & Safety, Risk, Enterprise Systems and Compliance) protects the company and powers the technology experiences of our global workforce. We're looking for a Senior Change Manager to own organizational change management (OCM) delivery and adoption strategy for CTREC's most critical programs — the changes that touch every Intuit employee, from security protocols to enterprise systems to employee-experience technology.
This is a hands-on leadership role, not an advisory one. You will craft the change strategy for each program and personally execute every piece of it — communications across channels, enablement content, stakeholder engagement, and adoption measurement. There is no separate design or communications team behind you, and no runway to learn the discipline on the job. Skilled, self-directed OCM leadership is essential to adoption success from day one.
You'll operate as part of the Change COE — the team that designs the human layer around technology change so employees don't just get access to something new; they understand it, want it, and can use it well. The COE matches its response to the size and risk of each change: it Drives the highest-impact changes end to end, Supports moderate ones by contributing strategy while the owning team executes, and Consults as the fast expert check on lower-risk changes. You'll flex across all three modes and partner with the OCM lead to define the engagement model and tiered level of support for each initiative.

Intuit has embraced a hybrid working model and this role will be based in office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities
- Own end-to-end OCM delivery and adoption strategy for critical CTREC programs — from impact assessment through launch, adoption, and reinforcement.
- Build change strategy from scratch and execute it end to end yourself: audience and impact analysis, adoption plans, success metrics, and risk mitigation — with no reliance on separate design or communications resources.
- Develop and deliver communications for multiple channels (email, Slack, intranet, in-tool messaging, executive briefings), right-sized to audience and moment.
- Create enablement content — guides, FAQs, training assets, self-service resources — that helps a distributed global workforce understand, embrace, and adopt change.
- Drive stakeholder engagement across all levels, from frontline employees to senior leadership, building the coalitions each change needs to land.
- Partner closely with Development, the Product lead, and the Technical Program Manager as an embedded member of the program team, and align strategy with the OCM lead.
- Flex across the Change COE's engagement tiers — Drive, Support, or Consult — matching depth of involvement to the size and risk of each change, and partner with the OCM lead to define engagement models and tiered levels of support across the portfolio.
- Invent creative, low-friction adoption solutions — resourceful ways to reach and activate distributed audiences and build trust in automation that acts on a user's behalf.
- Develop and implement change management tools and processes that accelerate change activities, ensure a consistent change experience, and standardize communication approaches across programs.
- Monitor employee feedback channels to address questions and gauge sentiment on Security change initiatives, feeding insights back into program decisions.
- Measure adoption, gather feedback, and iterate — closing the loop between user sentiment and program decisions.

Qualifications
- 7+ years of change management experience supporting large, multi-site enterprise implementations of HR, IT service, Security, or employee-experience technology.
- Proven ability to own change strategy from scratch and execute it end to end personally — you are the strategist, writer, designer, and facilitator in one.
- A track record of creative, low-friction adoption solutions that reached and activated distributed audiences — including building user trust in automation acting on their behalf.
- AI platform fluency — you use AI tools and platforms fluently in your own work (research, content development, analysis) and can guide others through AI-driven change.
- Excellent writing and content-design skills across formats and channels, with the judgment to right-size comms to the change.
- Strong stakeholder management — comfortable partnering with engineering, product, and program leaders and influencing without authority.
- Self-direction and speed: you scope ambiguity into a plan, prioritize independently, and deliver without needing the role explained to you.
- Strong proficiency applying ADKAR or an equivalent structured change methodology within condensed go-live timelines and high stakeholder expectations.
- Proven ability to manage concurrent workloads under a fixed deadline, sequencing communications across phased waves to prevent audience fatigue and message conflicts.
- Strong executive communication skills — comfortable drafting on behalf of senior HR and technology leadership for enterprise-wide distribution.
- Domain experience across collaboration SaaS applications, HR, and Security, with a working understanding of data security and compliance concepts.
- Skilled in impact analysis, stakeholder mapping, and developing communication and care/readiness plans.
- Technology company experience implementing change efforts that impact technologist/development organizations as well as business functions.
- Project management experience leading cross-functional teams to achieve business goals.

Who You Are
- Customer obsessed — inspired by the customer problem, partnering with process owners to drive change, education, and outreach.

- A strong process and systems thinker, sees how changes, channels, and audiences interact across a portfolio, and builds repeatable tools, standards, and mechanisms rather than one-off fixes.

- Demonstrates extreme ownership, delivers excellence at scale, and operates without boundaries.

- Influences and drives decisions by crafting a clear point of view — options, data-backed recommendations, and rationale — and builds a compelling, data-backed case for change.

- Proactively identifies obstacles, develops recommendations for resolution, and escalates to leaders quickly.

- Quickly establishes credibility and trust across teams; leads with inquiry and incorporates diverse perspectives to deliver high-impact outcomes.

- Resilient and solution-oriented in a high-change, often ambiguous environment, with a data-led and data-driven approach focused on long-term opportunity.

- Proactive, action-oriented self-starter with high judgment, innovation, and strategic thinking; strong organizational and time-management skills.

- Works independently and collaborates effectively across cross-functional teams and with employees at all levels, using inquiry and advocacy to work through barriers.

jobs.title: Principal, Strategy & Business Operations
jobs.description:
About Intuit
Intuit is a mission-driven, global financial platform company that gives everyone the opportunity to prosper. We do this by using technology to solve our customers' most important problems: putting more money in their pockets, eliminating unnecessary work and complexity, and helping them make financial decisions with confidence. Our flagship products, QuickBooks, TurboTax, and Credit Karma, reflect our commitment to transforming how people manage their finances, run small businesses, and pay employees. Intuit is a trusted partner to millions of small businesses and consumers, with a presence that is both broad and deeply rooted.

Who We Serve
Small businesses are the engine of the economy. In the U.S. they employ 60% of the workforce and create 80% of new jobs, yet most face long odds. QuickBooks exists to change those odds, giving small businesses the tools and confidence to manage their money, run their operations, and grow. It is Intuit's largest, most established business, and one of its fastest moving.

About the Role
Business Strategy and Operations (Biz Ops) exists to help define where we're going and help our teams focus on and execute against the most important work for QuickBooks. We do that in several ways: (1) shaping the strategy and vision for where we are going and what we want to achieve, (2) driving the rigor behind how we plan, (3) quarterbacking the highest impact work streams that cut across segments and functions, (4) building the operating systems that hold us accountable to what we said we would do, and (5) finding the next big bets before anyone else does.

We are hiring a Principal who can operate as both a senior strategic advisor and a hands-on builder: someone who can identify where QuickBooks should go next, shape that point of view with senior leadership, and personally drive the work that turns it into durable growth. This is an individual contributor role reporting directly to the Director of Strategy & Business Operations, QuickBooks Small Business and Platform, with the scope and visibility of someone operating at the center of the business: serving as a critical partner to our VPs of Product, Marketing, Sales, Finance, and Customer Success & Delivery, and becoming the person senior leaders come to for advice, fast clarity, and an unvarnished read on where things really stand.

This is a role for someone who wants to own outcomes, not just coordinate work. You will structure ambiguous problems, establish priorities, and personally engage in the most complex and high-impact work, whether that means uncovering the next growth vector before anyone else sees it, figuring out where AI can meaningfully change how QuickBooks serves small businesses, or building the operating system that turns a bold idea into a shipped outcome.

Responsibilities
What You'll Do

jobs.title: Principal, People M&A Lead & HR Business Partner
jobs.description:
Come join Intuit's People & Places organization as a Principal HR Business Partner, People M&A.

Acquisitions accelerate Intuit's strategic priorities, and their success depends on more than closing the deal: a clear People strategy, early identification of talent and workforce risk, disciplined cross-functional execution, and a transition experience that keeps incoming teams engaged and focused on delivering the deal's intended value.
In this role you are the senior People partner and accountable integrator for a portfolio of acquisitions and strategic transactions, leading the People workstream from early target assessment through due diligence, close, Day 1, and post-close integration. Partnering with Corporate Development, Legal, Finance, business leaders, aligned HRBPs, and People & Places centers of excellence, you translate each deal's thesis into an integrated organization, talent, rewards, and employee-experience strategy, and you own and evolve Intuit's People M&A Playbook so each transaction executes faster and better than the last.

You will not personally execute every functional activity. You set direction, mobilize partners, establish governance, drive decisions, surface risks, and ensure People commitments are delivered. You bring credibility with executives, frame issues in terms of business value and talent risk, challenge assumptions constructively, and operate with discretion and composure in confidential, ambiguous, time-sensitive environments.

Responsibilities
Lead the People workstream end to end
- Serve as the accountable People lead for a portfolio of acquisitions and strategic transactions, from early target assessment and pre-LOI planning through diligence, signing, close, Day 1, and post-close integration, often across multiple deals at different stages.

- Establish the People M&A operating model for each deal (workstream structure, decision rights, governance cadence, integrated plan, budget, and risk log), scaled to deal type, size, geography, and complexity.

- Mobilize and sequence specialists across People & Places COEs (HRBPs, Rewards, TA, People Ops, ER, HR Legal, People Systems, Payroll, Benefits, Immigration/Mobility, Workplace, Comms) and deal partners (Corp Dev, M&A Legal, Finance, Tax, IT, Security) so upstream decisions land before downstream execution begins.

- Maintain strict confidentiality and controls over deal disclosure, data-room access, and employee information.

Translate deal strategy into People strategy and diligence
- Partner with Corp Dev, Finance, Legal, and business sponsors to understand the deal thesis and value drivers, and build an integrated People strategy spanning org design, leadership, talent, workforce and location, culture, rewards, retention, and employee experience.

- Set an early integration hypothesis: what integrates at close, what incubates or transitions over time, and what must be preserved.

- Direct and synthesize People due diligence (org and talent, leadership and culture, comp and equity, benefits, ER and employment practices, labor and immigration, contingent workforce, payroll, HR systems and data, workplace) into clear risk assessments, cost estimates, and executive recommendations.

- Provide People inputs to the LOI, term sheet, purchase agreement, disclosure schedules, closing conditions, and retention arrangements; escalate material risks early enough to influence deal structure, valuation, or timing.

Shape the organization, talent, and acquired-employee experience
- Lead leadership, culture, and talent assessments; identify founders, executives, and deal-critical talent; and design short- and long-term org structures, reporting relationships, and workforce plans.

- Coordinate mapping of incoming employees into Intuit's job architecture and, with Rewards, Finance, Legal, and TA, develop compensation, equity, retention, relocation, and employment recommendations, ensuring decisions are documented, approved, and reflected in offers, data, and financial models.

- Own the end-to-end employee transition experience (announcement, change-impact assessment, communications, offers, onboarding, assimilation), with high-touch treatment for founders, executives, and deal-critical talent and appropriate handling of full-time, fixed-term, transitional, and contingent populations.

- Prepare managers and leaders to support incoming employees, and establish listening and escalation channels to catch experience breakdowns and retention risks early.

Ensure data, systems, and Day 1 readiness
- Establish a secure, reconciled single source of truth for employee, job, compensation, offer, and immigration data, with clear ownership, access controls, and privacy standards.

- Coordinate data migration and HR technology readiness across People Systems, Payroll, Benefits, TA, IT, Security, and external providers, including testing, cutover, exception handling, and post-close audit, so employees have pay, benefits, systems, and support on Day 1.

Drive post-close integration and value realization
- Govern the 30/60/90-day through 12-month People integration plan with business leaders and aligned HRBPs, covering org integration, leadership effectiveness, retention, culture, location strategy, and hiring.

- Track People outcomes (offer acceptance, critical-talent and overall retention, engagement, attrition, hiring progress, milestone and budget performance), connect them to deal value-realization measures with Corp Dev and Finance, and drive recovery plans when results are off track.

- Execute a structured handoff to aligned HRBPs and long-term functional owners with documented decisions, commitments, risks, and open actions.

Evolve the People M&A Playbook and capability

- Deploy the Playbook with judgment about what to expand, streamline, or omit per deal; run post-transaction retrospectives; and convert lessons into improved processes, templates, decision frameworks, dashboards, and data standards.

- Apply automation and AI-enabled tools to accelerate analysis, documentation, reporting, job mapping, and workflow while protecting confidential deal and employee information.

- Train and coach HRBPs, COEs, and deal-team members on People M&A roles, decision rights, confidentiality, and execution standards; during lower deal volume, lead M&A readiness, pipeline planning, and other strategic People initiatives.

Qualifications
Preferred Qualifications

- 5+ years directly leading People/HR M&A transactions across a range of deal types (talent, technology, operating-company, large-scale integration) and structures (divestitures, carve-outs, joint ventures, minority investments).

- Global or multi-country acquisition experience, including local employment requirements, consultation obligations, works councils, immigration, and cross-border compensation.

- Experience building a People M&A function, playbook, or governance infrastructure from the ground up.

- Background in management consulting, transaction advisory, or a corporate-development or enterprise integration-management office, ideally in a global, matrixed, technology-driven organization.

jobs.title: Principal, Corporate Strategy
jobs.description:
About Intuit
Intuit believes in the power of the individual. The power to do more. To make more. To be more.
We believe in the people who do things – the hat jugglers, the to-do list gurus, those who love getting it done faster, better, and more efficiently than ever before. Whether that's balancing the household budget, running a business, or paying taxes.
We believe in these people because we are these people. We thrive on action – and results. And by making things simpler, we all get more out of doing what we love. We're innovators and have been at it for more than three decades. And we don't stand still.
As the world evolves, so do we – inventing new solutions to solve important problems, perfecting those solutions, and delighting our customers. In short: We’re on a mission to power prosperity around the world.
We started small in 1983 with Quicken personal finance software, simplifying a common household dilemma: balancing the family checkbook. Today, Intuit is a leading provider of fintech solutions for consumers, SMBs, and the self-employed. You probably know us by our flagship products, TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp which serve over 100 million consumers and 20 million small businesses and self-employed across North America, Europe, Australia, and around the world.
Just as we transformed before, from DOS to the web, and to the cloud and mobile, we are evolving again to deliver personalized experiences on a trusted, open platform that helps create indispensable connections.
Supporting our mission, our strategy is to become an AI-driven expert platform and deliver three core benefits to our customers:
●        More money - helping put more money in the pockets of our customers
●        No Work - eliminating work and drudgery so they can focus on what matters to them
●        Complete Confidence - ensuring that they have complete confidence in every financial decision they make through our do-it-yourself or live expert support platforms
As the way we live and work evolves, we adapt our strategy to meet and lead these changes. We are committed to creating new and easier ways for consumers and businesses to tackle life's financial chores, giving them more time to live their lives and run their businesses. As our businesses and product lines grow beyond finance and accounting into new areas, we will build on our heritage of innovation. That's not just our history . It's our future.

Intuit’s Corporate Strategy and Development (CS&D) team is focused on defining and accelerating Intuit’s top strategic priorities. The team works on direction-setting strategy and acquisition initiatives at the corporate level and across all of Intuit’s businesses. The team advises and collaborates with Intuit’s most senior leaders, executive team, and Board of Directors to define both the company’s overall strategy as well as the strategy for specific business lines - with a strong focus on driving growth. jobs.title: Senior Technical Compliance Program Manager, LCPO Solutions & Strategy
jobs.description:
At Intuit, we help over 100 million people and businesses around the world feel more confident about their money. We are the proud makers of TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp. Our mission is to power prosperity around the world. We do this by staying customer-obsessed and using data and AI to solve the biggest financial challenges for our customers.
The Legal, Compliance, Policy Organization’s  Solutions & Strategy team is looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to join our team. As technical program manager, you will be part of a smart, collaborative team focused on modernizing how Intuit's legal function operates, leverages data, automation, and AI. In this role you will work closely with legal operations, counsel, engineering, and other internal stakeholders across the business to identify opportunities where technology and AI-powered tools can make LCPO faster, data driven, and more efficient while enabling the business.

Responsibilities
- Serve as a technical translator and point of contact between Legal, Compliance and Policy Practice Groups and FLP Tech engineering — converting legal/business requirements and processes into clear technical requirements, user stories, and program plans that engineering can execute against.
- Partner directly with LCPO stakeholders across Legal Practice Groups to gather requirements, ask the right clarifying questions, and surface the true underlying need,  not just the stated ask.
- Own end-to-end program delivery for prioritized Legal Tech initiatives (e.g., Unified Orchestration, workflow automation, AI-assisted review tooling, CLM and data lake integrations), from planning through launch.
- Champion end user experience throughout the delivery lifecycle — pressure-testing designs and workflows from the perspective of the legal/compliance  practitioners,and business stakeholders who will actually use these tools day to day.
- Structure program delivery across engineering teams by applying strong SDLC knowledge — identifying workstreams, owners, dependencies, and risks before they materialize.
- Drive the operating rhythm for assigned programs: build and maintain plans with clear milestones and success measures, run status/risk reporting, and proactively escalate blockers with recommended paths to green.
- Build credibility with technical SMEs and engineering leads — understand solutions deeply enough to participate in architecture and trade-off discussions, and communicate technical constraints back to legal/business stakeholders in plain language.
- Apply AI tools as thought partners to accelerate requirements analysis, documentation, and stakeholder communication, and help evaluate the quality and risk of AI-assisted outputs.
- Support change management for new tools, workflows, and process redesigns — including stakeholder communication, training, and adoption tracking — to ensure LCPO teams actually adopt what FLP Tech ships.
- Contribute to and help scale program management best practices, tools, and templates across the Legal Tech program portfolio.
- Own clear from-to metrics on intake so every request has a stated baseline and target before work begins.

Qualifications
- 5+ years of experience in technical program management, or a related program/product delivery role, ideally including some experience supporting enterprise, legal, compliance, or other regulated business functions.
- Strong working knowledge of SDLC methodologies and the software delivery lifecycle; able to structure and manage technical program delivery across cross-functional engineering teams.
- Demonstrated ability to act as a translator between non-technical business/legal stakeholders and engineering teams — turning ambiguous requirements into clear, actionable technical scope.
- Strong requirements-gathering skills, including the ability to ask incisive clarifying questions, identify unstated assumptions, and drive stakeholders to a well-scoped problem definition.
- High level of technical acumen: comfortable engaging in architecture and trade-off conversations with engineers, without requiring a hands-on coding background.
- A genuine focus on end user experience — able to advocate for usability and workflow simplicity even under legal/compliance complexity.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build trust and strong working relationships across Legal, Compliance, Privacy, and Engineering.
- Superior program/project management and time-management skills, including managing multiple priorities and cross-functional dependencies in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
- Proven ability to drive operating rhythm: building plans, tracking risks/dependencies, and communicating clearly with data to drive alignment and decisions.
- Familiarity with AI and automation tools (e.g., Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, agentic AI/workflow platforms) and a demonstrated interest in applying them to accelerate program delivery.
- Proven history of taking initiative, working independently, and proactively identifying areas of need and generating recommended action plans.
- Intellectual curiosity with a demonstrated willingness to dive into new legal, compliance, and technical domains.
- Preferred Prior experience working with or adjacent to a Legal, Compliance, or Privacy organization.
- Experience with legal tech / workflow orchestration platforms (e.g., Tonkean, ServiceNow, Ironclad, Legal Tracker) or comparable enterprise workflow tools.

jobs.title: Retail Operations Manager, TurboTax - Chicagoland Metro
jobs.description:
As a TurboTax Retail Location Manager, you'll be the driving force behind a high-performing, customer-focused local tax preparation center. With energy and purpose, you will lead a cross-functional team of motivated individuals, empowering them to deliver exceptional experiences to customers while ensuring operational excellence of the store. - Deliver constructive feedback and recognition that drives engagement and performance.
- Conduct performance reviews and set clear, motivating goals for each team member
- Foster a collaborative, high-energy culture where employees feel valued, supported, and inspired to deliver their best work.

Customer Experience & Advocacy:

Operational Excellence:
- Oversee all store operations, including scheduling, facility compliance, and technology troubleshooting.
- Ensure adherence to company policies, security standards, and regulatory requirements.
- Maintain an organized and welcoming store environment to facilitate efficient operations and an exceptional customer experience.

Store Performance Management:
- Own and manage the store’s P&L and key performance indicators (revenue, funnel conversion, operational efficiency, customer satisfaction.
- Analyze store-level customer feedback to identify service improvement opportunities and enhance the customer journey.
- Partner with corporate leadership to implement innovative strategies for revenue growth and operational excellence.

Community Engagement:
- Advocate for the store as a trusted, valuable community resource.
- Develop strong relationships within the local community to promote the TurboTax brand and establish the store as an accessible financial help center.
- Participate in local events or networking opportunities to attract and retain customers.

Tax Expertise:
- Leverage your deep understanding of taxes to personally support customer filings during peak periods or when team support is required.
- Guide Local Tax Experts through complex tax questions, leveraging your knowledge and expertise to ensure accurate, compliant filings.

Qualifications
- 3+ years in retail management, service industry leadership, or customer-facing leadership roles.

- Proven success managing KPIs and achieving operational benchmarks.
- Experience handling escalated customer complaints and delivering successful resolutions.

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer – SRE, Incident Response & Operational Excellence
jobs.description:
Intuit is the global financial technology platform that powers prosperity for the people and communities we serve. Our public-facing products — TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, and Mailchimp — serve approximately 100 million customers who depend on us at the moments that matter most: filing a return before the deadline, running payroll, checking their credit, or sending a campaign. When something breaks, minutes matter, and how quickly and how well we recover is a direct expression of our customer promise.
We are hiring Principal Software Engineers to serve as Technical Duty Officers (TDOs) — the leaders who take command of Intuit’s most critical incidents. During our most critical incidents you hold ultimate authority on decisions and enforcement of our incident principles, partnering with the Business Unit Driver and the Incident Operations Center (IOC) to direct recovery, actions, and communications on the bridge. Reporting to the Director of Cloud Engineering & Operations, this is a dedicated, full-time role: when you are not on the bridge, your mandate is to make the next incident shorter, rarer, and better understood — partnering across every business unit on effective observability, clarity of customer workflows and their real-time impact signals, high-quality runbooks, and validated escalation and notification readiness.

This role is equal parts operator, engineer, and leader. You bring the calm, decisive command presence to lead senior leaders through high-stakes ambiguity, the deep systems intuition to cut to the most likely fault and the fastest safe path to recovery, and the engineering skills to implement the improvements you identify rather than hand them off. As a Principal engineer, you will not just execute this work manually but direct, orchestrate, and govern AI agents to accelerate detection, triage, impact assessment, and post-incident learning, accountable for the quality and reliability of everything you and those agents produce.

Responsibilities

- Lead Intuit’s most critical incidents,  serve as the “Technical Duty Officer” role on all significant incidents, holding ultimate authority on decisions and enforcement of incident principles; direct recovery, actions, and communications on the bridge in partnership with the BU Driver and IOC Leader

- Drive fast recovery,  bias the bridge toward mitigation over diagnosis, make timely and decisive calls on rollbacks, failovers, traffic shifts, and feature disablement, and keep responders focused on the shortest safe path to restoring the customer experience

- Get the priority right early,  challenge and correct incident priority based on customer impact during active response rather than after recovery, and ensure the right leaders, escalations, and communications are engaged at the right time

- Establish clear customer-impact signals,  partner with each business unit to define, instrument, and continuously report real-time customer impact for the highest-value workflows across top revenue-generating products, and drive readiness validation through the company-wide Customer Impact Gameday

- Raise the observability bar,  partner with platform and product teams on SLOs, dashboards, alerting, and tracing so responders can assess the problem and its impact in minutes; feed tool and product-gap findings from live incidents back to platform teams as part of the RCA

- Own runbook and workflow clarity,  ensure critical customer workflows have accurate, exercised runbooks and clear service ownership, and drive the recurring validation of notification channels, escalation policies, bridge creation, and executive notification workflows

- Make communications actionable,  work with the IOC Leader so that executive and customer-facing updates consistently convey customer impact, recovery progress, and next steps with enough clarity for confident decision-making

- Lead post-incident learning,  drive blameless RCAs for the incidents you command, identify systemic and cross-BU remediation, and track high-leverage actions to closure

- Continuously improve incident and observability capabilities,  bring an SRE mindset to the incident-management and observability platforms, implement solutions yourself, and encode triage, impact-assessment, and communication knowledge into agentic and self-service tooling so standards travel with the automation

- Provide 24x7 coverage,  participate in the follow-the-sun TDO rotation across the US and IDC, including off-hours and peak-season (e.g., tax deadline, payroll) readiness windows, with clean shift handoffs

- Coach and scale incident leadership,  contribute to Incident Commander training for Directors, Distinguished Engineers, and Vice Presidents, mentor BU Drivers and responders on the bridge, and raise the incident-leadership bar across the company

jobs.description:
As Strategic Partnerships Manager: Analyst and Agency Partners, you own Intuit's commercial relationships with two distinct partner segments that sit at the edges of the mid-market ERP ecosystem: independent ERP analysts, and digital marketing agencies whose client base includes mid-market businesses evaluating ERP solutions.

ERP analysts in the mid-market are not the large research firms — they are independent voices: channel consultants, software selection advisors, and influential commentators who cover mid-market ERP platforms, shape buyer decisions, and maintain active networks of prospects and VARs. They generate a steady flow of referral introductions to buyers who trust their judgment. Building relationships with the right analysts and turning those relationships into a consistent pipeline of qualified warm introductions is the core of this motion.

Digital marketing agencies represent a different but equally valuable opportunity. Many agencies serve mid-market clients who need ERP solutions as part of broader digital transformation work — and those agencies need somewhere to route those leads. This role builds the program and relationships that make Intuit the natural destination for those introductions.

Both motions share the same KPI: qualified warm introductions attributable to a specific analyst or agency partner. You are not accountable for closed-won revenue — you are accountable for the quality and volume of the pipeline you generate through these relationships.

PRIMARY KPI: Qualified warm introductions attributable to a specific analyst or agency partner — defined as a mid-market prospect introduction where an IES, QuickBooks Advanced, or Intuit Services opportunity has been identified. Measured separately for analyst and agency segments.

jobs.description:
People and Places technology is shifting from system-driven workflows to agentic, platform-enabled execution. AI agents increasingly drive how work gets done. Most efforts to date have focused on automating low-value tasks; the larger opportunity is to reimagine — not simply optimize — how work happens across People & Places.
We are looking for a manager to lead this reimagination. This role owns identifying the highest-value P&P workflows to redesign, partnering with COEs and HRBPs on what work should look like in an AI-first model, and translating that into agentic workflow patterns enabled through HR Tech, T4I, and strategic vendor partnerships. This is the center of excellence for AI-driven People & Places transformation: the team defines end-to-end workflows, decision points, and employee and candidate experiences, then partners with HR Tech and the Agentic Builder team to bring them to life.
Success on this role is not just throughput. While this work is expected to drive a 3x productivity gain across P&P, the deeper measure of success is whether employees, candidates, and managers experience meaningfully better interactions with HR — faster and clearer where it matters, and invisible where it doesn’t need to be seen at all.

Responsibilities

Workflow Reimagination & Opportunity Identification
- Systematically identify and size the highest-value P&P workflows for agentic reimagination, prioritizing high-cost, high-demand functions such as HRBPs, TA, and employee support

- Build and maintain a prioritized roadmap of workflow redesign opportunities across People & Places

COE & HRBP Partnership
- Partner with COEs, HRBPs, TA, Rewards, Talent, ER, Mobility, and People Analytics under a “build from the center, drive from the spokes” model — enabling, not gatekeeping, their own innovation

Agentic Workflow Design & Standards

Team Leadership
- Lead and integrate the merged Process & Experience Design team, combining the former Experience Solutions and Process Excellence functions into one cohesive capability

Measurement & Scaling
- Define and track metrics for both productivity (progress toward 3x) and employee/candidate experience quality
- Establish a scalable operating rhythm for prioritization, delivery, and adoption of reimagined workflows across People & Places

jobs.title: Director, HRBP - Expert Network
jobs.description:
Intuit is a global platform company on a mission to power prosperity around the world for consumers, the self-employed, and small and midmarket businesses. Across our four leading brands — TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, and Mailchimp — Intuit serves over 100M customers and is one of the few companies in the world to have a thriving consumer and small and midmarket business ecosystem. Intuit is known for its innovation track record, customer centricity, and its consistent recognition as a top place to work. Year-over-year, Intuit is recognized as a best employer and consistently ranked on Fortune's '100 Best Companies to Work For' and Fortune World's 'Most Admired Software Companies' lists.
Intuit's Customer Success organization includes the Expert Network (EN). EN is the AI-driven virtual expert platform connecting millions of customers across the Intuit ecosystem to the digital and human-assisted expertise they need to make confident financial decisions. EN has evolved from a tax-focused experiment into the world's largest expert network, with nearly 50,000 product and domain experts across six countries, a mix of full-time and seasonal tax experts, year-round SelectTime experts, and third-party product experts. EN is now driving two transformative shifts at once: deepening AI agent integration that is fundamentally reshaping how the network operates and serves customers, and 'Activate Local Experts,' a national retail/local strategy that will place roughly 1,100 new employees at local sites across the country and is a key driver of Intuit's revenue growth.
This hybrid role will focus on the Expert Network business within the Consumer Group and will be based out of our beautiful San Diego, California office.
Why this role, now
Intuit is rebuilding how work gets done. We're moving to AI-native leadership — where AI carries coordination and synthesis, and leaders spend their time on judgment, coaching, and culture. We're aligning business strategy directly to the skills, scale, and shape of our teams. And we're driving AI adoption company-wide, so every employee can deliver stronger outcomes with more velocity.
Our People & Places function sits at the center of this transformation — not enabling it, leading it. Our HR Business Partners are embedded members of Intuit's most senior executive teams: growth accelerators, executive coaches, and change agents who shape business strategy, not just the talent plan behind it. We operate as business leaders first — fluent in the P&L, the operating model, and the competitive landscape — who happen to lead through people.
This role demands exactly that. You'll sit shoulder-to-shoulder with the executive team, own the leadership and organizational bets that determine whether we win, and coach senior leaders through the most significant reinvention of work in a generation.

Responsibilities
Responsibilities
- Business partner, first: Understand the Expert Network's strategy, economics, and operating model deeply enough to proactively define and shape the talent strategy, priorities, and in-year outcomes with the senior executive team.

- Executive coach: Serve as a trusted advisor and coach to the senior executive team — build trust, be courageous with coaching and feedback, and unlock leadership potential in the era of AI.

- Cross-functional builder: Partner across HR functions — talent acquisition, compensation, talent development, and manager training — to design and stand up the people systems and infrastructure needed to scale a network of this size, not just support existing structure.

- Talent steward: Partner with leaders and talent acquisition to identify, develop, and hire senior talent, with AI-first expectations built into hiring rubrics and goals from the start. Build the capability for others to do the same — attracting, hiring, and retaining top talent.

- High-performing team builder: Build high-performing senior executive teams, and through them, highly engaged, high-performing organizations that deliver on the Expert Network’s vision and strategy. Leverage team effectiveness strategies to drive prioritization, x-functional alignment, and velocity.

- Culture carrier: Work with the senior executive team to role model the behaviors and values that create a high-velocity culture where employees — whether seasonal, year-round, or site-based — do their best work and have fun while doing it.

- Change agent: Drive and accelerate Intuit-wide priorities such as AI-powered work and strategic workforce planning across Expert Network. Partner closely with the People & Places centers of excellence on career growth, mobility, executive development, manager training, and total rewards, especially as they apply to a large hourly, seasonal, and geographically dispersed population.

- Data-led operator: Leverage AI tools and dashboards to turn quantitative and qualitative people data into insights and actions.

Qualifications

- 10+ years in senior HR leadership, partnering directly with executives on business results, not just HR process.

- Experience with workforce planning and org. design — building org. structures, career frameworks, and staffing models for a business scaling headcount quickly, not just optimizing an existing org.

- Strong business acumen — able to interpret operating and financial performance, follow strategy, and translate both into talent and organizational decisions that influence business outcomes, not just structure.

As Talent Acquisition analytics has moved past descriptive reporting, this lead position will drive overall TA analytics strategy focusing on hiring forecasting, talent funnel conversion modeling, and defining and delivering AI-native use cases and prototypes across data & analytics. This role plays a key part in supporting major HR initiatives, including workforce planning and organizational effectiveness. This individual will build trust in TA's data, both in Avature and in the data lake, and translate that trust into a strategic understanding of the talent data ecosystem that strengthens TA's ability to meet business hiring needs and deliver on operational excellence.

This is not purely a technical role. It requires the business acumen and leadership presence to connect insights across the full candidate and employee lifecycle - bringing hiring, attrition, and internal mobility together - and to operate as a trusted advisor to TA leadership, shaping the questions as well as answering them. It also means bringing an external lens into TA: benchmarking Intuit's hiring funnel, forecasting approach, and recruiter productivity against industry standards, so TA's methods keep pace with where the broader market is headed. Working across the broader People Analytics team, you will partner on Talent Acquisition data products, analytics, and models combining hands-on analysis with the advisory judgment to turn findings into decisions.

Responsibilities
Data & Analytics Roadmap Design & Execution
- Translate TA and business strategy into analytical problems, self-generating hypotheses from the data and validating or disproving them to produce recommendations that inform hiring and workforce decisions across multiple initiatives.
- Develop, maintain, and socialize the Talent Acquisition Data & Analytics roadmap, reflecting a prioritized inventory of the current and upcoming work, and drive the business case for the investments it implies.
- Define the metrics that hold TA and business leaders accountable for hiring strength and requisition governance, at the function level rather than the individual report level.
- Combine insights, business acumen, and strategic considerations to influence Director-level and above stakeholders, translating complex analysis into a narrative leaders will act on rather than simply report against.
- Connect insights across the candidate and employee lifecycle, bringing hiring, attrition, and internal mobility together into a single view.
- Bring external analytics benchmarking and TA industry best practices into Intuit, so forecasting, funnel, and recruiter-productivity work is informed by where the broader market and competitors are heading, not only by internal history.

Strategy and Measurement for AI-Native Experiences
- Ideate and scope AI use cases within Talent Acquisition by connecting industry-wide developments in AI with strategic insight, customer knowledge, and TA domain knowledge, from ideation through measurement.
- Influence cross-functional partners in creating a development plan for those use cases, and define success metrics that connect model performance to hiring and business outcomes.
- Provide thought partnership on phased testing and rollout of AI-native experiences, with the right measurement in place at each stage.
- Drive requirements for scaled solutions including automated insights, dashboards, and reporting that support TA leadership, recruiters, HR, and Finance.

jobs.description:

About the team
Intuit's Business Intelligence (BI) team builds the reporting and analytics experiences that millions of QuickBooks customers and accountants rely on every day, including Modern Reports, Management Reports, KPI Scorecards, Dashboards, and FP&A (Cash Flow, Budgets, Forecasting). The team is in the middle of extending these experiences with AI: conversational reporting through Omni, self-serve report building, and agentic development practices that let us build faster on a codebase spanning years of financial logic. We sit on one of Intuit's largest proprietary datasets, tens of billions of transaction rows across millions of small businesses, and we are scaling our platform (built on StarRocks) to support multi-entity, multi-currency customers at a new order of magnitude.
About the role

As a Staff AI Scientist on BI, you will be a technical leader spanning multiple BI workstreams, such as Core Reporting, Multi-Entity/Scale, and Conversational Narrative Builder. You will architect AI-native systems and evaluation frameworks that other AI Scientists across BI build on, and you will help set the direction for how BI uses agentic AI to serve accountants and

Responsibilities

- Serve as a technical leader across multiple BI workstreams, influencing product and technology direction beyond a single team.

- Architect AI-first systems for BI, such as agentic reporting assistants and dimension-aware forecasting engines, including systems where LLMs orchestrate tools and skills across the BI surface area.

- Build Intuit's AI advantage in BI by deeply leveraging our proprietary financial data (tens of billions of transaction rows across millions of businesses), instituting comprehensive evaluation and monitoring across both traditional and agentic BI systems, and applying novel combinations of ML methods.

- Lead creation of reusable, versioned data and feature assets from BI's data platform (built on StarRocks) and set data-quality bars for downstream science and product work.

- Architect multi-stage agent pipelines spanning the BI science lifecycle, from data preparation through experiment execution to results synthesis, that other AI Scientists across BI can build on.

- Champion responsible AI practices given the sensitivity of financial data and the accuracy required for customer- and accountant-facing insights.

- Partner with BI product, design, and engineering leadership to frame ambiguous problems, such as how conversational AI should explain multi-entity consolidated statements, and co-own end-to-end customer solutions.

- Coach and elevate other AI Scientists and engineers across BI, help them direct and orchestrate agents on real work, and identify tooling or process gaps that block productivity.

Qualifications

jobs.title: Principal Analyst - Credit Risk Management, Intuit Business Credit Card
jobs.description:
One out of every two small businesses fails within their first five years, most often due to running out of cash. QuickBooks Capital is on a mission to make a dent in that statistic, by providing small businesses access to the capital they need when they need it, leveraging the data inside QuickBooks for faster and better decisioning. This way, our customers never again have to worry about not making payroll or saying no to a business opportunity. That’s how we power prosperity.

QuickBooks Capital is a nimble and high-priority business unit within Intuit that is looking to reinvent small business borrowing. We are the fastest growing SMB lending business in the market. We are looking for top talent and team members that love new challenges, cracking tough problems and working cross-functionally. If you are looking to join a fast-paced, innovative and incredibly fun team, then we encourage you to apply.

As a key leader of the Credit Risk Management team for Intuit’s business credit card product, you will be responsible for developing, optimizing and managing strategies for credit card underwriting, risk-based pricing, portfolio management, debt collections and loss forecasting.  You will provide a strategic vision for growing product adoption by leveraging test and learn agendas, life time valuations based decisioning and risk prediction models. You will be responsible for developing and maintaining the credit policy for all stages of the product life cycle, and will be accountable for program performance.

You will lead a team of analysts to set analytical agendas by identifying business priorities, framing key risk questions, and translating them into clear analysis roadmaps for the team. You will identify business problems that require modeling solutions and collaborate heavily with the Data Science team in the development and deployment of risk and performance prediction models. You will be an active proponent of leveraging AI and automation in developing analytical insights, updating models and deploying strategy changes.
You will effectively partner with multiple cross-functional teams to implement and monitor strategy changes across the card lifecycle. You will partner heavily with the marketing team to identify prospects from Intuit’s vast customer base and drive customer acquisition efforts. This is a high visibility leadership role that presents an excellent opportunity to grow an analytical team through hiring, mentoring and developing talent.

Responsibilities
- Develop, implement and manage credit risk management strategies across customer targeting, underwriting, portfolio management, collections and drive overall card profitability
- Leverage cashflow analyses and other business data of Intuit’s Quick Books customers to enhance underwriting and overall risk management
- Develop A/B tests to help understand credit risk/return tradeoffs using hypothesis testing frameworks

jobs.title: Group Manager -Payments Business Development & Partnerships - QB Payments
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Intuit is the global financial technology platform that powers prosperity for the people and communities we serve. With approximately 100 million customers worldwide using products such as TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, and Mailchimp, we believe that everyone should have the opportunity to prosper. We never stop working to find new, innovative ways to make that possible.
Getting paid faster is one of small business owners’ most critical problems. Cash flow challenges are cited as a cause for 82% of small business failures, and this remains an unsolved problem despite rapid innovation in fintech. QB Payments is core to solving it: we currently process $175B of the $2T in invoices sent across the QuickBooks platform, having grown at a 40% CAGR since our 2017 platform investment.

Job Overview

FY27 is a pivotal year for QB Payments. We’re pursuing several major initiatives to accelerate Total Payment Volume and deepen our role in how small businesses get paid. At the same time, the broader payments landscape is shifting quickly — card networks, acquirers, fintechs, frontier LLM’s are racing to define agentic commerce, stablecoin rails, and embedded finance, all of which intersect directly with QuickBooks’ own ambitions.
We are looking for a Head of Payments Partnerships to lead this agenda. This position requires strong strategic problem-solving and communication skills, the ability to influence and develop productive partnerships at all levels of the organization, and a strong understanding of Intuit’s mission and values. This is a role with broad exposure to senior leaders across GBSG and the Services Segment.
You will lead a team, reporting to the Director of Business Development, and work closely with our Payments leadership, Product, Commercial, Engineering, Risk, and Ops teams to address our customers’ AR problems and accelerate growth.

The Opportunity

QB Payments sits at the center of Intuit’s Center of Money strategy, and partnerships are a primary lever for both defending and extending our position. You will own the full partner portfolio across several active and emerging fronts:
•         Payment ecosystem partners — card networks, acquirers, wallets, and alternative payment methods that expand acceptance, reduce settlement costs, and improve approval rates
•         Embedded finance and BNPL — building on the Affirm partnership model to expand financing options at checkout and improve conversion for higher-ticket transactions
•         AI and agentic commerce — positioning QB Payments and QBO as the system of record inside emerging agent-mediated transaction flows (e.g., MPP/ACP-style protocols), as card networks, Stripe, and others race to define this space

•         Ecosystem integration partners — working with AP and adjacent software providers to remove seams across the customer's broader tech stack, ensuring a seamless payments experience regardless of which tools a QB business uses to run its operations

Responsibilities
Own the Partnership Lifecycle
•         Lead full-cycle business development for our payments business, QB Payments
•         Build and manage a pipeline of high-priority partnership opportunities with rigor and velocity
•         Develop and maintain executive-level relationships with key partner counterparts
•         Oversee ongoing partner management, strengthening relationships with key payment partners and resolving escalations with the appropriate internal teams
Set and Influence Strategy
•         Define the multi-year partnership strategy for the payments business, including prioritization frameworks, partner segmentation, and go-to-market models
•         Drive the strategy and prioritization of key partnership initiatives, including structuring and negotiating new opportunities
•         Develop clear points of view on build vs. buy vs. partner decisions, and bring well-structured recommendations to Payments and GBSG leadership
•         Proactively identify whitespace opportunities at the intersection of Intuit’s SMB and Mid-Market customer base, data assets, financial products, and partner distribution capabilities
•         Act as a subject matter expert on payment trends, rules, and regulations, sharing insights with internal stakeholders and tracking fast-moving developments across agentic commerce, stablecoin infrastructure, and embedded finance
Drive Cross-Functional Execution

•         Collaborate with Risk and Finance to structure deals that are commercially sound, risk-policy aligned, and poised for accelerated growth
•         Work with Marketing to develop co-marketing and co-distribution playbooks, and elevate QB Payments’ influence in the ecosystem through joint product development and strategic initiatives
•         Coordinate with Legal and Compliance on deal structuring, data-sharing frameworks, and regulatory considerations
•         Support Quarterly Business Reviews with key merchants by providing insights on payment partnerships and developments
Operate as a Senior Leader
•         Lead and develop a team responsible for managing and expanding our payment partnerships, with a proven ability to mentor and build high-performing talent
•         Represent the Payments BD function in cross-GBSG forums, including the QB Product Partnerships annual planning process
•         Foster strong cross-functional collaboration across global teams including Product, Engineering, and Commercial
•         Deliver executive-ready outputs: one-pagers, strategy briefs, and board-quality narratives that clearly articulate opportunity, tradeoffs, and path to value

Qualifications
Experience

•         Demonstrated track record of sourcing, structuring, and closing complex, multi-party partnership agreements — not just managing existing relationships
•         Experience negotiating with payments ecosystem partners, including card networks, acquirers, wallets, payment methods, fintechs, risk tech, and gateways

•         Comfortable working across commercial, product, and technical discussions, and operating in global, cross-functional environments

Strategic & Analytical Strength

•         Commercially minded, with experience structuring partnerships and negotiating agreements
•         Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate data into actionable insights and recommendations

Communication

jobs.title: GBSG Customer Success - Staff Data Scientist
jobs.description:
The GBSG Customer Success Data Science & Analytics team's mission is to empower world-class customer experiences across digital and expert-led channels by delivering data-driven insights, experimentation, and predictive intelligence. We partner closely with Customer Success, Product, Data Engineering, and Operations teams to improve customer engagement, retention, and long-term success across Intuit's Services businesses—Payroll,  Payments, and Bill Pay—for small and  mid-market  customers.
As a Staff Data Scientist supporting Services, you will serve as a senior individual contributor and strategic thought partner, applying deep analytical expertise and business judgment to some of GBSG CS's most complex and high-impact problems. You will shape measurement frameworks for expert-led and human-assisted success motions, lead advanced experimentation and causal analysis, and translate insights into clear recommendations  that influence strategy and execution  across the  organization.

This role offers a unique opportunity to help define how Customer Success and expert-services impact is measured at scale—especially as Intuit evolves its data platforms, AI-enabled and human-in-the-loop  experiences,  and customer engagement  models across  the Services portfolio.

Responsibilities
- Serve as a strategic analytics partner to Customer Success, Services, Product, and Operations leaders—helping define problems, success metrics, and data-informed decisions across Payroll, Payments, and Bill Pay.
- Conceptualize ambiguous business problems, formulate hypotheses, and design rigorous analytical approaches to evaluate Customer Success and expert-services programs (e.g., CSM coverage, outbound and inbound-friction motions, 'Nail the Basics').
- Design, execute, and interpret experiments beyond traditional A/B testing, including causal inference methods (e.g., quasi-experiments, DiD, matching, synthetic control) to isolate the incremental impact of human-assisted success motions.
- Develop and maintain scalable measurement frameworks for key CS and Services outcomes such as engagement, retention, share-of-wallet, TPV growth, customer health, and support effectiveness.
- Build predictive models and durable customer segmentation approaches to improve targeting, prioritization, and CSM assignment across the Services customer base.
- Size and prioritize customer-friction and revenue-risk opportunities, turning analysis into clear, actionable roadmaps for Services leadership.
- Apply modern AI tooling to accelerate the analytics workflow—using LLM-assisted development environments (e.g., Cursor, Claude) and internal AI/MCP capabilities to move faster from question to insight, while holding a high bar for correctness and reproducibility.
- Design and evaluate AI/ML- and LLM-powered customer experiences, building the measurement and causal frameworks that determine whether agentic and human-in-the-loop success motions actually move customer and business outcomes.
- Translate complex analyses into clear, actionable insights and narratives for both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including senior leadership and cross-functional Services partners.
- Partner with Data Engineering to ensure high data quality, well-defined metrics, and scalable analytics assets—especially during platform and data migrations.
- Champion analytics rigor, experimentation best practices, and reusable solutions that scale impact beyond individual projects.
- Role-model Intuit's 'Win Together' mindset by collaborating deeply across teams and elevating the  analytical bar  of the broader organization.

Qualifications
- 8+ years in data science, analytics, or product analytics, with demonstrated impact in customer success, product, or go-to-market domains.
- Deep foundation in advanced analytics: causal inference and quasi-experimental design (DiD, matching, synthetic control, regression discontinuity), statistical modeling, and experimentation well beyond simple A/B testing—including knowing which method fits an ambiguous, real-world business question and defending the choice.
- Predictive modeling and segmentation experience—building models (propensity, churn/retention, LTV, customer health) that are used in production decisions, not just one-off analyses.
- Advanced SQL and strong Python for analysis, modeling, and experimentation (pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, statsmodels).
- Working fluency with modern AI tooling for data science—using LLM-based coding assistants (e.g., Cursor, Claude) and AI/agent workflows to increase speed and quality, with sound judgment about where AI accelerates the work and where human rigor must own the result.
- Proven ability to work with large, complex datasets and translate insights into business decisions.
- Excellent communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders.
- Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science, or related); advanced degree preferred.

jobs.title: Principal Marketing Manager, Media Investment Intelligent Decisioning
jobs.description:
Intuit's Consumer Group (CG), a team serving the needs of over 30+ million US consumers to file their annual tax returns, is looking for a Principal Marketing Manager, Media Investment Intelligent Decisioning.

This role sits at the center of how TurboTax makes investment decisions. You will own the partnership between Paid Media, Data Science, and Finance that determines channel mix and investment allocation across the TurboTax envelope, and you will run the weekly SLT Investment Review that translates model output and marketplace signal into a clear point of view for senior leadership. In parallel, you will help build the Central Decision Engine — the architecture that unifies MMM, platform, and creative signal into a single, always-on source of investment guidance — moving the team from weekly reporting to real-time, model-driven decisioning.

This is both a strategic and a builder's role. You will need to be equally comfortable defending an investment recommendation in front of the SLT and contributing to the data architecture that produces it. The Principal Marketing Manager will report to the Director of Paid Media.

What You'll Bring

Strategic, Analytically Grounded Communicator
- Ability to translate complex model output — MMM curves, channel mix tradeoffs, marginal ROI — into a clear, channel level direction and executive-ready narrative, both written and verbal

- Comfortable owning and driving a recurring analytics and finance forum, a channel reporting and guidance forum and a senior leadership forum. This includes setting the agenda, anticipating questions, and proposing / defending a strategic recommendation.

- Strong point of view, backed by data — someone who forms and influences a recommendation

Cross-Functional Influence
- Proven ability to build durable, high-trust partnerships with Data Science and Finance — functions with different incentives and different definitions of 'right' — and align them to a shared investment view

- Skilled at managing up and across a matrixed organization without formal authority over the teams you depend on

- Able to represent Paid Media's interests in cross-functional forums and instilling confidence

Integrated Media & Budget Management Fluency
- Deep working knowledge of an integrated media environment spanning search, programmatic/digital media, social, video, streaming, and above-the-line channels, and how investment shifts in one channel affect performance in another

- Experience managing a large media investment envelope: forecasting, in-season reallocation, marginal curve analysis, and defending spend decisions with data

- Understands how agency partners (search, digital media, ATL) operationalize a channel mix decision once it's made

Builder's Mindset
- Excited by the opportunity to help design and build a system, in an evolving AI led evolving media enviorment

- Comfortable in ambiguity — defining architecture and process where none currently exists, in close partnership with Paid Media and GTM leadership

Responsibilities
Investment Decisioning & Data Science / Finance Partnership
- Own the operating partnership with Data Science and Finance on investment decisions and channel mix — translating MMM output, incrementality findings, and marketplace signal into a shared point of view on where dollars should go

jobs.title: Principal Partnerships Manager, Payments
jobs.description:
Money movement is one of Intuit's fastest-growing businesses — the engine behind every card payment, ACH transfer, real-time payment, instant deposit, bill pay, and cross-border transaction that flows through our platform. Behind each of those transactions is a network of partners: card networks, acquirers and processors, sponsor banks, payment networks, digital wallets, and risk and compliance providers. The terms, economics, and resilience of those partnerships directly shape how fast we grow, how healthy our margins are, and how good the experience is for tens of millions of customers.

The Principal Partnerships Manager, Payments owns that entire partner ecosystem — sourcing, structuring, and negotiating the external relationships, and orchestrating the internal alignment across Engineering, Product, Business Development, Legal, and Data Science needed to turn each deal into real, measurable value. This is a senior individual-contributor role with outsized scope: you'll operate everywhere from the boardroom to the contract redline to the launch dashboard, in a business where the partner landscape and regulatory backdrop are moving fast — and where your decisions have direct, visible impact on Intuit's growth.
We're looking for a strategic, commercially sharp, and results-driven partnerships leader to define and execute Intuit's money movement partner strategy. You'll own a portfolio of our most critical payments partners, go out and source new relationships that expand what we can offer and improve our economics, and act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership on build-vs-buy-vs-partner decisions across the money movement value chain.

This role sits at the intersection of high-stakes external negotiation and high-influence internal leadership. You'll negotiate directly with partner organizations, and you'll lead — without direct authority — the cross-functional effort across Product, Engineering, Business Development, Legal, Finance, Treasury, and Data Science that brings each partnership to market and scales it. Few roles in fintech offer this level of end-to-end ownership over how money actually moves for a platform this size.

Responsibilities

- Define, own, and execute the multi-year partnership strategy for payments and money movement, aligned to growth, margin, speed-to-market, and risk objectives. Continuously evaluate build vs. buy vs. partner tradeoffs and bring new perspectives on how to achieve product and business goals.

- Source, structure, and negotiate complex commercial agreements across the money movement ecosystem — card networks, acquirers and processors, sponsor and partner banks, ACH/RTP/FedNow and other payment rails, wallets, and KYC/fraud/risk providers — securing favorable economics and terms while building durable partner relationships.

- Serve as the end-to-end owner of priority third-party partnerships: develop joint business plans, define launch strategy, and monitor performance against KPIs including payment volume, attach, authorization and approval rates, cost per transaction, and partner-driven revenue.

- Drive internal alignment across Engineering, Product, Business Development, Legal, and Data Science — on integration and roadmap requirements, company-wide partner strategy, deal structure and risk, and partner economics and opportunity sizing — so every team is working from the same playbook on each partner.

- Act as a trusted thought partner to executive leadership, delivering market intelligence, partner benchmarking, and data-driven recommendations that guide investment and prioritization decisions.

- Manage partner economics and commercial performance over the life of the agreement — renegotiating terms, resolving escalations, and identifying opportunities to expand partnerships into new capabilities, rails, and markets.

- Proactively monitor the competitive, regulatory, and risk landscape across money movement, translating shifts into strategy and contingency plans that keep Intuit ahead of the curve rather than reacting to it.

Qualifications

- 10+ years of overall experience with significant time spent in partnerships, business development, or strategic alliances, with direct experience in payments, money movement, or financial infrastructure strongly preferred.

- Deep, demonstrated understanding of the payments value chain and money movement economics — card networks, acquiring/processing, sponsor banking, ACH and real-time rails (RTP, FedNow), interchange, and the risk/compliance considerations that govern them.

- Proven track record of independently sourcing, structuring, negotiating, and closing complex, multi-faceted partnerships with large strategic enterprises and financial institutions that delivered significant and quantifiable results.

- Experience managing a portfolio of strategic partners, including building joint business plans, tracking performance against KPIs, and consistently exceeding growth and margin targets.

- Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functionally through influence — aligning Engineering, Product, Business Development, Legal, and Data Science partners around shared outcomes without direct authority.

- Strategic mindset, strong business acumen, and a data-driven approach, with the ability to navigate ambiguity, regulatory complexity, and rapid change in a high-growth environment.
